quandoUsar: Showing at which prices trading concentrated in a session or a few sessions, alongside how the price moved over time.
Highlighting the point of control, the level with the most volume, and the value area, which by default gathers 70% of the volume around it.
Reading each price band with its volume, share of the total, and position relative to the value area, by pointer or arrow keys.
quandoEvitar: Use `candlestick-chart` when the focus is the open, high, low, and close of each period.
Use `order-book` for the depth of open buy and sell orders, not for what has already traded.
Use `bar-chart` for volume per period, such as per day or per hour; here volume is grouped by price.

teclado.acao: With focus on the chart, move up to the next price band.
Move down to the previous band.
Move up or down four bands.
Go to the lowest or highest price band.
Ends the reading and hides the tooltip.

acessibilidade: The chart is a vertical `role="slider"`: on receiving focus by keyboard it starts at the point of control, and `aria-valuetext` reads the band, the volume, the share of the total, and whether it is in the value area.
The `<figure>` has a hidden caption and a hidden table with all bands, from highest to lowest, with volume and share; the SVG, header, and tooltip are hidden from screen readers.
The read-out phrases and the header (`point of control`, `Inside the value area`, `Value area`) are hardcoded in English; `formatPrice` and `formatVolume` change only the numbers.
movimento: On entering the viewport, the bars grow from the axis, starting at the point of control and spreading to the farthest levels, while the price line draws from left to right.
After that, new data doesn't repeat the entrance: bars, line, and the point-of-control mark glide on a spring, and a series with a different number of points redraws the line from the start.
With “reduced motion” on, everything appears in its final state, and the highlighted band and the tooltip jump from one level to the next.
responsivo: The width follows the container: the histogram takes 32% of it (between 64 and 190 px), the price line takes the rest, and a fixed 62 px column on the right holds the prices; the height is `height` (260 px).
On touch, tapping at a height reads that band; dragging vertically scrolls the page and ends the reading.
desempenho: The price line is rebuilt on every render, including when the pointer changes band; with thousands of trades, aggregate into intervals first, as the demo does with 5 and 15 minutes.
notasIA: Pass `data` in time order with `{ key, label, price, volume }` and `axisLabel` on only some points; each point adds its volume to the band the price falls in, and `levels` (16) sets how many bands there are.

`valueArea` (0.7) is the fraction of volume that forms the value area; `formatPrice` and `formatVolume` format the axis, header, and tooltip, and `hideHeader` hides the title with the point of control.
`activeLevel` with `onActiveChange` controls the band being read, counted from the lowest price (0), or `null` for none; without control, `defaultActiveLevel` sets the initial one.
